clue.text: Presenting bill with credit-notes after collapse is wrong

indicators.note: the bill and credit-notes are placed after the word for collapse

parts.note: to collapse is to fall
AC is short for account, a bill
IOUs are notes acknowledging a debt, credit-notes

explanation.surface: Someone who presents a bill and some IOUs after a business collapse is in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' sets the bill and credit-notes behind the collapse, though the clue names the bill first. IOUs are written promises to pay, hence notes of credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallacious argument is mistaken or misleading, so it is plainly in error.

clue.text: Complaint of the cat's-paw — unlike a certain queen

explanation.surface: A dupe grumbles, in contrast to a famously unsmiling monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A cat's-paw is a person exploited by another, whose complaint would be 'I am used'. Queen Victoria is famously quoted as saying 'We are not amused', so to be the opposite of her is to be entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the letters give the exploited person's grumble 'am used'; whole, they describe someone entertained, the reverse of Victoria's legendary verdict.

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost their timetable has also stopped paying attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking energy or interest describes someone inattentive; read literally, the word is 'without a list', a list being a schedule.

clue.text: Many not of nice disposition can appear sweet

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many

indicators.note: disposition here means arrangement, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of people who are not nice by nature can still seem charming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals that NOT OF NICE is rearranged into ONFECTION, after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection is a sweetmeat, an item of confectionery.

parts.note: O is round in shape
per means for each, as in per head
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: A labourer doing his rounds is paid at so much per insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Operant means operating or producing an effect, that is, in action.

explanation.surface: A picture taken during a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick casual photo is a snapshot; Snap is also a children's card game in which matching cards are called out.

clue.text: Perhaps a pill consumed so to alleviate disease

indicators.note: Perhaps suggests the letters of the next words might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: consumed food means ate

explanation.surface: A tablet swallowed to ease an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that A PILL is rearranged to PALLI, followed by ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease the symptoms of an illness without curing it.

parts.note: to quail is to flinch, to wince
still in the sense of even now, yet
TE is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Fill a game bird with stuffing, and keep it quiet, please note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' and 'quail' suggest cooking a game bird, but quail is a verb (flinch) and stuff is a noun meaning cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Winceyette is a soft brushed cotton cloth, and stuff is an old word for woven fabric.

clue.text: The Italian, a writer, backing a man in the Himalayas

indicators.note: backing means the pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An Italian author supports a mountaineer in the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IL, A and PEN together, giving NEPALI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nepali is a native of Nepal, the country containing much of the Himalayan range.

clue.text: A hint about the first person seen beginning to cause trouble

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the hint goes round the other letters

parts.note: a nuance is a subtle hint or shade of meaning
I is the first person pronoun

indicators.note: beginning picks the opening letter of the word seen

explanation.surface: A subtle sign around the first person to be spotted starting to make problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I and S (the start of 'seen') inside NUANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance is a source of annoyance or bother.

parts.note: re means concerning or regarding
public means open to everyone

explanation.surface: Interested in wide-open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open country' reads as a single phrase for moorland, but 'open' belongs with the wordplay and 'country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation governed without a monarch.

clue.text: To make a gradual, oblique advance is an advantage.

definitions.text: To make a gradual, oblique advance

explanation.surface: Creeping sideways forward gives you the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch sideways towards something is to sidle; having a slight lead over a rival is having the upper hand.

clue.text: Former copper's a Conservative and apologetic for it

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the 's adding an S
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An ex-policeman has joined the Tories and is sorry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Excusatory means offering an excuse or justification, making an apology for something.

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is the one Ariel sings of in Act 2 of The Tempest, a wide-awake plot against the sleeping Gonzalo

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Shakespeare's The Tempest with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ariel's song to the sleeping Gonzalo runs 'While you here do snoring lie, Open-eyed ... His time doth take', warning of the plot by Antonio and Sebastian.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song the missing word is the plotters' scheme, a secret plan to murder the king.

clue.text: Feature of ways used by BR — or of certain waves?

definitions.text: Feature of ways used by BR — or of certain waves?

parts.words: Feature of ways used by BR — or of certain waves?
parts.note: British Rail's track is the permanent way, and a perm is a permanent wave in hairdressing: both share the quality of lasting

explanation.surface: A characteristic shared by railway tracks and some hairstyles.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway; its track is called the permanent way. A perm is a permanent wave, a lasting curl set in hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The shared adjective in both phrases is the quality of lasting, here turned into a noun.

definitions.note: the definition is possessive: one of Flora's, a flower belonging to the Roman goddess of flowers

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so cows
a slip is a woman's undergarment

explanation.surface: A girl called Flora has tidy lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the archaic word for cattle. Flora is the goddess of flowers, so one of Flora's is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula, a plant belonging to Flora, goddess of flowers.

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the word for court

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: development suggests the word Later evolving into a new form

explanation.surface: A later twist in a legal case at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb meaning to pursue romantically. 'development' scrambles the first word, giving ATERL, and 'in' places that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo was the 1815 battle in which Napoleon was finally defeated.

explanation.surface: A shout of attendance at roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: Present means in attendance at this place, and also existing at this moment rather than past or future.

parts.note: a skinhead has had the hair taken off the scalp, and one who danced naked performed a striptease, so both senses fit

explanation.surface: A shaven-headed youth danced in the nude.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare of covering describes both a shaven head and a dancer who has peeled off clothes.

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the rearranged word
strange suggests the word castle is made unfamiliar by rearranging it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A hospitable resident of an odd fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges CASTLE into ELASTC, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means flexible or adaptable, readily stretching to suit circumstances.

indicators.note: unrestrained letters are set free to move, so the word Australian is rearranged

explanation.surface: Wild Aussie and Roman revelry.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten letters of AUSTRALIAN rearrange exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saturnalia was the ancient Roman December festival of feasting and licence.

explanation.surface: Someone stood, dressed as a female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up as a woman' suggests dressing in drag; 'got up' is the past tense of getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, to stand or climb out of bed; Rose is also a woman's first name.

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the next piece below, so after the word for hit

parts.note: to slog is to hit hard

explanation.surface: Lighting upon a fitting expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit on' reads as stumble upon, but it splits: 'on' in a down clue sets the second piece below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a short memorable motto or catchphrase.

clue.text: Sits with reel, spinning, never wearying of it

indicators.note: spinning sends the letters of the previous words whirling into a new order

explanation.surface: An angler sits with a fishing reel turning, never tiring of the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an angler; 'spinning' is the signal to scramble the first two words' letters, and 'of it' completes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tireless person shows unflagging energy, never flagging.

parts.note: these organs take in nothing but noise; sound reads as healthy but means audible vibration

explanation.surface: Their consumption is perfectly healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' suggests healthy, so the clue seems to praise a diet; really it is the noise these organs take in.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of hearing receive only noise, nothing else.

clue.text: Guys may well get attached to them

definitions.text: Guys may well get attached to them

parts.words: Guys may well get attached to them
parts.note: guys here are guy ropes, which are fastened to stakes in the ground, not men forming attachments

explanation.surface: Men often grow fond of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' suggests men, but guys are the ropes that steady a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Guy ropes holding a tent upright are tied to stakes driven into the ground.

clue.text: As disturber of the peace one has to err badly

indicators.note: one has the letters around it, so it sits inside the rearranged phrase
badly suggests the words to err are mangled into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is bound to make mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TO ERR into ROTER, with I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking part in a violent public disorder is a breaker of the peace.

explanation.surface: Coming first and coming next.
explanation.definitionFit: Succeeding means achieving success, so triumphing; it also means coming after, as one reign succeeds another.
